title: Browser Back/Forward navigation fails for pages with special characters in pathname
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When using MPAv2 pages whose `url_path` contains non-ASCII characters (for example `á`, `ê`, `ã`), Streamlit fails to restore the page correctly during browser Back/Forward navigation and falls back to the app root page instead.

ASCII-only routes work correctly under the exact same conditions.

This appears to be caused by inconsistent handling of encoded vs decoded pathnames.


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

pg = st.navigation(
    [
        st.Page(
            lambda: st.write("Home"),
            title="Home",
            url_path="home"
        ),
        st.Page(
            lambda: st.write("Wíth Spêcîãl Chäracters"),
            title="Wíth Spêcîãl Chäracters",
            url_path="Págé_Wíth_Spêcîãl_Chäracters",
        ),
        st.Page(
            lambda: st.write("Without Special Characters"),
            title="Without Special Characters",
            url_path="Without_Special_Characters",
        ),
    ]
)

pg.run()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

### Control case (works correctly)

1. Open the "Without Special Characters" page
2. Navigate back using the browser Back button
3. Navigate forward again using the browser Forward button

Result:

* Navigation works correctly

---

### Failing case

1. Open the "Wíth Spêcîãl Chäracters" page
2. Navigate back using the browser Back button
3. Navigate forward again using the browser Forward button

Result:

* Streamlit fails to restore the page
* The app falls back to the root/home page instead

### Expected Behavior

The following encoded pathname:

```text
/P%C3%A1g%C3%A9_W%C3%ADth_Sp%C3%AAc%C3%AE%C3%A3l_Ch%C3%A4racters
```

should correctly resolve back to:

```text
Págé_Wíth_Spêcîãl_Chäracters
```

during browser history restoration.

### Current Behavior

During browser Back/Forward navigation, Streamlit fails to resolve routes containing unicode/special characters and falls back to the root page.

ASCII-only routes continue to work correctly.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.57.0
- Python version: 3.14.5
- Operating System: Windows
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

Browsers normalize unicode pathnames into percent-encoded URLs.

For example:

```text
/Págé_Wíth_Spêcîãl_Chäracters
```

becomes:

```text
/P%C3%A1g%C3%A9_W%C3%ADth_Sp%C3%AAc%C3%AE%C3%A3l_Ch%C3%A4racters
```

during navigation/history restoration.

This issue appears related to route matching between encoded and decoded pathnames.

Direct navigation can work initially, but Back/Forward restoration fails.

JavaScript example:

```js
// Works correctly
window.history.pushState({}, '', '/Without_Special_Characters');
window.dispatchEvent(new PopStateEvent('popstate'));

// Fails and falls back to the root page
window.history.pushState({}, '', '/Págé_Wíth_Spêcîãl_Chäracters');
window.dispatchEvent(new PopStateEvent('popstate'));
```
